usage: Planning concept only; not a sprite sheet or verified production palette.
selectionReason: The initial board was too detailed for the requested low-resolution style. The simplified variant better establishes large silhouettes and sparse backgrounds.
constraintsForProduction: Author final sprites on a consistent pixel grid with a measured four-color base palette, no gradients, integer scaling, and distinct combat telegraphs. The generated board does not certify these constraints.
generationPrompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: original low-resolution pixel-art game concept board, not a finished game screenshot. Create a wide 3:2 landscape concept board for a tiny portrait-mobile timing-action boss-rush game, working title The Last Bellkeeper. No text whatsoever. Three equally sized portrait scenes side by side, separated only by narrow dark gutters: left is a ruined gate at dusk with a tiny hooded bellkeeper carrying a small lantern and a short hammer, facing a simple hollow armored guard; middle is the interior of a tall abandoned bell tower with broken gears, a giant cracked bronze bell above, the same tiny hero facing a hanging chain creature; right is the open summit at pre-dawn with one huge dark bell-shaped sentinel and the hero, a tiny amber light beginning to return to the horizon. This is extremely SIMPLE LOW-RESOLUTION pixel art, readable big pixel blocks, as if rendered at 120x200 pixels per scene and nearest-neighbor scaled. Hero roughly 16x24 source pixels, enemies roughly 32x40 source pixels, clear silhouettes, sparse background detail, hard edges, no antialiasing, no gradients, no painterly lighting, no glossy illustration, no intricate pixel noise. Limit entire scene to 8 colors: near-black charcoal, navy, two desaturated slate blues, pale bone, muted bronze, warm amber, single bright golden hit accent. Side-on one-versus-one battle composition, enemy on right, hero on left, feet on common ledge. Keep lower 25 percent of each scene simple dark negative space for eventual controls, no controls or letters drawn. Tiny sharp amber sparks near the hero suggest a precise dodge-and-counter. Emotional mood: lonely but hopeful, cute readable small character, mild fantasy combat, no blood. Original characters, no borrowed game sprites, no logos, no watermark. The appeal is clean silhouette, visible attack anticipation and very low asset complexity.
finalEditPrompt: Edit this concept board. Preserve the three side-by-side portrait scenes, the tiny hooded lantern hero versus a guard / chain ghost / bell sentinel, the navy-and-amber mood, and the lower blank control area. CHANGE ONLY THE VISUAL COMPLEXITY, making the art dramatically simpler and much LOWER RESOLUTION. The current image is far too detailed. Treat every portrait scene as an actual 90 pixel wide by 160 pixel tall old handheld game screen, then enlarge every pixel as a crisp visible square. Giant visible pixel blocks, about 16 screen pixels per logical pixel. Hero should be only about 8 pixels wide and 12 pixels high in the low-res source. Enemy only 18 pixels wide and 26 pixels high. FOUR FLAT COLORS ONLY for the entire board: near-black navy, muted slate blue, parchment cream, amber gold. Flat filled silhouettes with only one accent area; no textured metal, no shading, no dithering, no gradients, no bloom, no thin lines, no tiny details. Background in each panel is almost empty: only a simple arch in left, a simple bell suspended from one horizontal beam in middle, and a crescent with one distant tower in right. Flat dark bottom area. Cute, crude and deliberately minimalist old four-color handheld game aesthetic, not elaborate pixel illustration. Absolutely no text, logos, UI or lettering.
